correctness.rationale: On a saturated disk coordinate the exact inward criterion is a strictly negative radial real part; equality cannot illuminate because the quadratic norm increment is then nonnegative. Both saturated coordinates give open half-circles in angle space. A direction simultaneously inward on two saturated coordinates works for the corresponding point with one nonsaturated coordinate as well by continuity, for small positive time. For the torus lower bound, 2r open half-arcs cannot r-cover: integral equality would force count r almost everywhere, while any starting endpoint loses at least one arc relative to the adjacent right cell. At each horizontal slice this requires at least 2m+1 active squares, whose second-coordinate arcs then require at least 4m+3 squares. With N=4m+3, an open half-circle contains at least 2m+1 consecutive starts of the regular grid even at an endpoint. Their doubled second starts have minimum cyclic gap 2/N and closing gap 3/N. Any closed half-circle contains at most m+1 such points, since m+2 would force span ≥2(m+1)/N>1/2; the complementary open half-circle therefore contains at least m. This proves the upper bound without discarding square edges or intersections. The two phases with offsets −1/4 give exactly the two specified open angular intervals.

residual_risks: The replay is finite; the closed-complement argument proves the all-multiplicity assertion. The lower bound relies on openness and includes repeated directions with multiplicity.
